item.title: Sports Focus: Wuhan Open spurs spending boom
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
The Wuhan Open attracted a record 202,700 spectator visits and generated an estimated 890 million yuan in economic benefits, highlighting how major sporting events can boost tourism, consumer spending and grassroots tennis development beyond the tournament itself. by sportswriters Yue Wenwan and Yu Xi WUHAN, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- For years, when Vietnamese businessman Dang Phu visited China in autumn, his destination was always the Canton Fair. This year, he and two colleagues arrived three days earlier than usual to watch some of the world's best women's tennis players in action. "We wanted to see top players compete in person and experience the atmosphere," Dang said. The Wuhan Open, the season's final WTA 1000 event, was held at the Optics Valley International Tennis Center from Oct. 10 to 18, drawing 105 players from 38 countries and regions. In previous years, the tournament coincided with "Golden Week," the weeklong Chinese National Day holiday in early October that drives a surge in travel and shopping across China. This year, the event fell outside the holiday period, yet it drew a record 202,700 spectator visits, 52,700 more than last year. An assessment by organizers put the tournament's overall economic benefits at about 890 million yuan (around 133 million U.S. dollars), up 26.24 percent from a year earlier. Dang's detour reflects how professional sports are creating new reasons for people to travel and new opportunities for cities to attract consumers beyond traditional holiday peaks. TENNIS FUELS TOURISM Much of the tournament's appeal comes from a growing community of fans who follow the sport beyond their hometowns. According to organizers, visitors from outside Wuhan accounted for 48 percent of this year's spectators. At the Wuhan Open, spectators could be seen carrying rackets and wearing tennis outfits, with some arriving with plans to play as well as watch. Cui Guorong, a tennis enthusiast from Chengdu in southwest China, bought tickets for three days with her doubles partner. Afterward, they planned to travel to nearby Xianning for an amateur event organized by the International Tennis Federation. Cui has built her travels around tennis in recent years, watching tournaments in London and Paris, as well as in cities across China, including Beijing, Shanghai, Huangshan and Wenzhou. "I came here both to watch matches and to play," Cui said, who practiced tennis in the morning and watched professional players in the afternoon and evening sessions. "At my age, there are some techniques I can't master myself, but watching these players still gives me inspiration, and is a pleasure in itself," she added. For fans like Cui, the Wuhan Open is more than a ticketed event. It becomes the centerpiece of a trip, with practice sessions and amateur competitions extending their stays and spending in the region. FROM MATCH TICKETS TO SHOPPING BAGS Local authorities and businesses have been working to harness the enthusiasm and spread its economic benefits beyond the stadium. Hubei Province issued 20 million yuan in consumer vouchers, while Wuhan offered another 10 million yuan in sports vouchers. Other initiatives included tennis-themed travel itineraries, discounts for visitors presenting match tickets and live screenings in shopping districts. Outside the tennis center, a fan festival covering about 10,000 square meters brought together more than 100 stalls selling sports equipment, local specialties, food, drinks and other goods. At a stand for Tim Hortons, the Canadian coffee chain, drinks passed through the service window one after another as customers queued in long lines. "The tournament offered an opportunity to boost both sales and brand recognition," said Wang Xiuping, the brand's regional operations manager for Hubei and neighboring Hunan province, adding that the successful try in Wuhan encouraged the company to participate in more sporting events in China. At a temporary Wilson store, customers crowded around displays of tennis rackets, comparing models and seeking advice. Some out-of-town visitors arranged to have their purchases shipped home. Sales at the store rose 10 percent from the same period last year, said Ye Xiufeng, who managed the stall. The tournament's reach also extended into the evenings. Large screens in major shopping centers broadcast matches alongside amateur tennis challenges and other activities. Organizers said the "second-screen venues" attracted 12 million visits and generated nearly 300 million yuan in consumer spending during the event. BUILDING A MARKET BEYOND NINE DAYS The longer-term question is whether a major tournament can do more than create a temporary spending surge. An amateur team competition held alongside the Wuhan Open at the same tennis center offered one answer. As Latvia's Jelena Ostapenko faced a British opponent in the tournament's semifinals, three outdoor courts nearby hosted the finals of the Wuhan Open city club circuit, an amateur team competition that has been running for more than a decade. The circuit held qualifying events in seven cities this year, drawing more than 2,100 players from about 150 clubs across China. Liu Fen, president of Wuhan's Chongren Tennis Club, whose team finished second, said playing on the same grounds as world-class athletes brought a special sense of pride. "As amateur players, sharing the same grounds with the world's top players fills us with a tremendous sense of fulfillment and pride," Liu said. She has witnessed how the sport has grown in Wuhan over more than a decade. Her club started with just one court and a dozen members. "After Li Na won her Grand Slam title, more and more people started playing tennis. After Zheng Qinwen won Olympic gold in 2024, the number of players grew many times over, and courts began springing up everywhere," Liu said. The club now has 365 members, more than 100 of whom gathered at the tournament venue each day during the Wuhan Open. "For local tennis amateurs, Wuhan Open is an annual celebration. The exciting matches and warm atmosphere make us want to come every day. We often start watching at 11 a.m. and stay until 11 p.m.," Liu said. The enthusiasm is already carrying into next year. After the club circuit's finals, members began preparing for the next edition. "Everyone is even more motivated after this year's finals. We hope to have more teams reach the finals next year and show the world what amateur players like us can do," Liu said. ■

item.title: China-Europe freight train service tops 140,000 trips
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
A freight train loaded with containers departs from Puhe station in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, Oct. 22, 2026. A China-Europe freight train bound for Moscow departed Puhe station in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, at around 11:30 a.m. Thursday, bringing the service's cumulative trips to top 140,000 and transporting goods worth over 560 billion U.S. dollars since 2011. Within China, 96 scheduled routes for trains traveling at 120 km per hour link 132 cities along the western, central and eastern corridors, while overseas the network now runs on three lines: northern, central and southern. Together they reach 237 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 12 Asian countries, covering most parts of Eurasia, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway), the national rail operator. The southern route is now operating on regular basis, running 746 trains in the first nine months of 2026, up 125 percent year on year. (Xinhua/Pan Yulong) SHENYANG, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- A China-Europe freight train bound for Moscow departed Puhe station in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, at around 11:30 a.m. Thursday, bringing the service's cumulative trips to top 140,000 and transporting goods worth over 560 billion U.S. dollars since 2011. The milestone comes a decade after the service adopted the unified brand of China Railway Express in June 2016. Annual trips rose from 1,702 in 2016 to 20,022 in 2025, an average annual increase of more than 30 percent, according to the National Development and Reform Commission. A single month's volume now equals the whole of 2016. As a flagship project and a landmark brand of the Belt and Road Initiative, the China-Europe freight train service, also referred to as the "steel camel caravans," has established a comprehensive logistics network across Eurasia. Within China, 96 scheduled routes for trains traveling at 120 km per hour link 132 cities along the western, central and eastern corridors, while overseas the network now runs on three lines: northern, central and southern. Together they reach 237 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 12 Asian countries, covering most parts of Eurasia, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway), the national rail operator. The southern route is now operating on regular basis, running 746 trains in the first nine months of 2026, up 125 percent year on year. In May, the service set a monthly record of 1,965 trains and 197,000 TEUs. An official with the logistics center of China Railway said the operator has been advancing infrastructure connectivity and the alignment of standards and rules to build a smooth, efficient, multi-directional network that links rails with sea routes. ■ A freight train loaded with containers departs from Puhe station in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, Oct. 22, 2026. item.title: Vietnamese student bridges China and Vietnam through traditional Chinese medicine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
Vietnamese student Lam Quang Duong (L) practices acupuncture under the guidance of his mentor, Dr. Chen Manghua, at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi University of Chinese Medicine in Nanning, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Oct. 21, 2026. Lam enrolled to the university in 2019 and completed his undergraduate studies in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). Now he is pursuing master degree in acupuncture and tuina. Coming from a family of medical professionals, he chose a different path from his family members, most of whom practice Western medicine. His goal was to become the first TCM practitioner in his family. Fluent in Chinese, Lam believes that TCM is not only a medical skill, but also a means of cross-border cultural exchange and heritage preservation. After graduation, he plans to return to Vietnam to practice medicine and continue his clinical and academic work in TCM. "I want to contribute to the medical development of China and Vietnam and help promote the exchange and preservation of traditional medicine between two countries," he said. item.title: China's millennial porcelain hub revitalizes ancient craftsmanship with global innovations
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
* The 2026 China Jingdezhen International Ceramic Expo was held from Oct. 18 to 22 in Jingdezhen, a city famed as China's "porcelain capital." The five-day event attracted more than 1,000 professional buyers from home and abroad. * With a porcelain-making history spanning more than 1,000 years, Jingdezhen developed a sophisticated handicraft industry that connected raw materials, specialized artisans and kiln production. * Today, the city is building on its legacy by bringing together traditional artisans, international artists and young innovators to explore how ancient skills can remain relevant in contemporary life. NANCHANG, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- Glimmering in appetizing colors, a stall filled with lobsters, crabs and sea urchins stands out among the teaware and decorative pieces at the Spring and Autumn Fair in Jingdezhen, east China's Jiangxi Province. Created by Kenyan artist Megan White, the porcelain artworks reflect the sights and culture of her coastal homeland, which she has brought to China's famed porcelain hub through the city's centuries-old craft. "I grew up on the coast of Kenya, so I'm constantly inspired by and drawn to the sea," she said. She has spent 20 months in Jingdezhen. Using local porcelain and techniques such as slip casting, White transforms familiar marine life into sculptural works that invite visitors to appreciate the ocean from a city far from the sea. White's stall offers a glimpse into Jingdezhen's evolving ceramic scene, where international artists are drawing on traditional craftsmanship, while introducing new cultural perspectives and creative ideas. With a porcelain-making history spanning more than 1,000 years, Jingdezhen has developed a sophisticated handicraft industry that connects raw materials, specialized artisans and kiln production. On July 25, 2026, the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites, representing the city's historic porcelain-making system, were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Today, the city is building on this legacy by bringing together traditional artisans, international artists and young innovators, exploring how ancient skills can remain relevant in contemporary life. TRADITIONAL TECHNIQUES REFORGED For White, Jingdezhen's appeal lies not only in its long history but also in the dedication of its craftspeople. "The dedication and precision associated with the local ceramic craftsmanship are very inspiring," she said, adding that local artisans encourage her to strive for the same standards in her own work. Unlike the red clay traditionally used for pottery in Kenya, porcelain has become the primary medium for her creations in Jingdezhen. She makes molds from her own designs and produces her pieces by hand, combining her personal artistic language with techniques developed in the Chinese porcelain-making tradition. White said she values such traditional crafts in a mass-producing era, even though they require considerable time and expertise. "Once these traditions disappear, we can't bring them back." China is making a tremendous effort to keep traditional techniques alive, she said, adding that this is what has compelled her to learn and innovate in Jingdezhen. For Dutch artist Antonetta Eilers, meanwhile, Jingdezhen offers room to experiment with new forms and ideas. Working with porcelain and jewelry, Eilers draws inspiration from nature and the sea, while collaborating with a friend whose artistic concepts explore possible futures shaped by climate change and environmental transformation. Eilers said she is struck by the local creative atmosphere, where an unexpected result does not need to be discarded but can become part of an artwork. She said the city's artist residency programs are helping visiting artists exchange ideas and develop their own styles and skills. "Techniques evolve, and I think that evolution is actually a form of preservation in itself," she said. The growing presence of international creators is part of a broader creative ecosystem in Jingdezhen. According to Gao Xiaoyun, deputy mayor of the city, Jingdezhen has gathered more than 3,400 inheritors of intangible cultural heritage, over 100,000 young creative entrepreneurs, around 60,000 newcomers from other parts of China, and more than 5,000 foreign residents at peak times engaged in its ceramic community. This mix of experienced artisans and emerging creators is helping traditional techniques find new practitioners and new applications, ensuring that heritage is not confined to workshops and exhibition halls. TECH-INFUSED CREATIONS While handcraft remains central to Jingdezhen's identity, technology is opening up new possibilities for ceramic production. At a local porcelain enterprise, 65 industrial-grade ceramic 3D printers demonstrate how digital design can be translated into intricate forms. The technology enables the production of customized vases featuring complex curves, hollow structures and textures that can be difficult to achieve through conventional techniques. "3D printing allows for a wider variety of ceramic forms and more intricate textures," said Hong Ziyu, the company's general manager. The technology, he added, has helped meet growing demand for customized decorative products. The company's 3D-printed porcelain products have gained traction in overseas markets, generating annual sales of more than 5 million yuan (about 750,000 U.S. dollars), according to Hong. Such developments reflect a wider transformation in Jingdezhen's ceramic industry. From 2021 to 2025, the industry's output value rose from 51.6 billion yuan to 102.7 billion yuan, while the number of major industrial enterprises above the designated size increased from 140 to 298, according to local statistics. For young creators, the convergence of traditional craftsmanship, digital tools and commercial opportunities is also creating new career paths. Digital modeling and advanced manufacturing can help artists test ideas and produce distinctive designs, while the city's network of workshops and specialized suppliers supports the transition and commercialization from concept to finished product, supporting a booming creative industry. Xu Wan, manager of Chentian Ceramics company in Jingdezhen, said the firm is collaborating with numerous pop culture IPs to draw Gen-Z customers, which is boosting the firm's sales. Xu said the company has collaborated with the hit animated film "Nobody" in launching a series of intangible cultural heritage-themed ceramic blind boxes in 2025, with the product quickly becoming a sought-after hit among young collectors after its release. "Young consumers today are more than willing to pay for creative products highlighting emotional value," Xu said, adding that they have released dozens of innovative products beyond trendy toys, including ceramic speaker boxes and night lanterns. SUPPORTING GLOBAL CRAFTSMANSHIP With talented artists and a booming creative ecosystem, Jingdezhen's international appeal has extended beyond the works created within its workshops. Japanese ceramic artist Shusaku Kanzaki, who has visited the city three times, said Jingdezhen has helped him find a larger audience for his artworks. Drawing on historical techniques and aesthetics, some of Kanzaki's pieces use no glaze, relying instead on the effects of wood firing to create their color and texture. Such Karamono-styled creations have won the hearts of many connoisseurs during the 2026 China Jingdezhen International Ceramic Expo held from Oct. 18 to 22. Kanzaki said that combining tradition with new ideas is essential to creating compelling works of art. Simply reproducing old objects, he argued, is not enough to sustain the craft. The abundant ceramic inspirations and support from local friends and authorities have made Jingdezhen an appealing place for him to explore, he said. Beyond artists, the city's experience is also attracting interest from other ceramic-producing regions, which are confronting challenges in passing on traditional skills. During a visit to the expo, Witthayalak Samjai, a senior deputy administrator of Chiang Mai, a city in northern Thailand, said she is learning from Jingdezhen's experiences to vitalize Chiang Mai's traditional Lanna ceramic arts. Some experienced Lanna ceramic artisans remain reluctant to depart from traditional styles, and their products are often made as decorative gifts rather than everyday objects, making it difficult to reach modern consumers, she said. Jingdezhen's integration of tradition, contemporary design and market applications offers lessons for northern Thailand, she said. Ilada Junjiresrassamee, vice president of the Lampang Province Chamber of Commerce in Thailand, said a local university's ceramics program in Lampang, which had run for 35 years, was suspended for three years amid waning interest among young people. Inspired by Jingdezhen, local stakeholders plan to revive the program and introduce hands-on workshops for children, she said. Jingdezhen has established friendly ties with more than 180 cities in 72 countries, using international exchanges to promote dialogue and cooperation in ceramic culture, according to Gao, the vice mayor. Following the inscription of the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites on the UNESCO World Heritage List, the city has also called for stronger global cooperation on heritage conservation. In concurrence, a multilateral initiative issued at the 2026 Jingdezhen Forum has called for respect for cultural diversity, the use of digital tools for preventive conservation, the integration of traditional techniques with contemporary design, and closer collaboration in talent development and research. For a city whose porcelain once traveled across continents, its global connections now encompass not only finished products but also creative ideas, technical expertise and shared approaches to heritage protection. In the view of Tim Winter, a professor at the National University of Singapore and president of the Association of Critical Heritage Studies, the challenge is to keep the exchanges alive, preserving the skills that give porcelain its character while allowing new generations, from Jingdezhen and beyond, to shape what the craft can become. ■

item.title: China's activities in Arctic are in line with international law: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China's activities in the Arctic, aimed at promoting the peace, stability and sustainable development of the region, are in line with international law, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Thursday. Mao made the remarks in response to a related query noting that the EU's new Arctic strategy identifies China's growing presence in the region and its cooperation with Russia as security concerns. Mao said the Arctic bears on the common interests of the international community, and countries' rights and freedoms to carry out activities in the Arctic in accordance with the law need to be fully respected. "Dividing countries into blocs out of Cold War mentality and inciting geopolitical confrontation are not in the interest of peace, stability and development in the Arctic region," she added. ■

item.title: World Insights: Growing practical cooperation boosts China-Russia ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
MOSCOW, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China-Russia trade has topped 200 billion U.S. dollars for three consecutive years, with China remaining Russia's largest trading partner for 16 years -- a sign of the economic momentum underpinning their deepening ties. From Russian agricultural products reaching the dining tables of Chinese households to Chinese-made automobiles traveling on streets in Russia, practical cooperation between the two countries continues to deepen, injecting vitality into the growth of bilateral ties. VIBRANT COOPERATION Today, China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination is at the highest level in history, setting an example for relations between countries. Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said on Wednesday that despite mounting external pressure, Russia-China trade and economic cooperation is gaining strong momentum: mutual trade has increased more than 30-fold over 25 years. Cooperation in investment, energy, cultural and humanitarian fields is developing steadily. Interregional ties are being consistently strengthened and, most importantly, people-to-people contacts are expanding, Mishustin added. According to Chinese Ambassador to Russia Zhang Hanhui, two-way trade from January to August this year reached 185 billion dollars, up by 28.4 percent year-on-year, and a full-year figure is expected to hit a new all-time high. "The share of local currency settlement in China-Russia trade has exceeded 99 percent. Cross-border e-commerce volume has surpassed 40 billion dollars, and the platform economy boasts enormous potential. Energy cooperation is advancing steadily. Russia remains a major crude oil supplier to China, with a marked rise in supplies of liquefied natural gas. Dividends from the mutual visa-free policy keep unlocking. Russia has become the second-largest source of foreign tourists to China," Zhang said. Moreover, high-tech manufacturing sectors have become highlights of bilateral cooperation, with expanded areas in artificial intelligence, logistics, finance, energy, science and technology, agriculture and healthcare. Aisen Nikolayev, head of Russia's Republic of Sakha, told Xinhua that the republic is a key implementer of Russia's "Pivot to the East" strategy and an active participant in Russia-China regional cooperation. Its cooperation with Chinese provinces and municipalities spans trade, energy, logistics, science and technology, innovation and other areas, with bilateral trade with China surging 52 percent year-on-year in the first five months of 2026. Dmitry Bakanov, head of Russia's state space corporation Roscosmos, said the cooperation agenda between the two countries covers several topics, including joint work on the lunar mission and the Mars mission. HEART-TO-HEART BONDS Beyond growing economic ties, China and Russia are also deepening their friendship through cultural exchanges to foster greater mutual understanding. China was the Guest of Honor at the 39th Moscow International Book Fair held in September. Under the theme of "Reading China," more than 2,000 titles and nearly 5,000 books were displayed. During the Guest of Honor program, the Chinese side hosted over 40 cultural events, including a China-Russia civilization exchange forum, copyright negotiations, new book launches, and dialogues between writers and scholars. "Many Russians have begun reading Chinese novels. In particular, numerous online novels have gained great popularity after being translated into Russian. This serves as a direct reflection of the steadily warming relations between China and Russia," said Xie Xiaocheng, director of the International Exhibition Center at China National Publications Import and Export Group. "Chinese literature delivers a wealth of emotions and adventures all at once," Maria Rudneva, editor-in-chief of Freedom, an imprint of Russia's leading publishing house Eksmo, told Xinhua. In the eyes of publishers and readers, Chinese works offer more than entertainment; they open a window to Chinese culture and classical Chinese literature for Russian readers, who have shown demand for new Chinese stories. This summer, Moscow hosted its first-ever Wushu Festival, drawing more than 30,000 spectators and roughly 830 athletes from multiple Russian cities. "Wushu (martial arts) is deeply loved in Russia. I am confident that this festival will serve to further popularize it, drawing more and more people, young and old, into this beautiful art and sport," said Sergey Sanakoev, deputy chairman of the Russian-Chinese Friendship Society. Close people-to-people exchanges are also reflected in education. At present, Chinese language courses are available at 360 schools across Russia, with more than 100,000 Chinese learners. Maria Zvereva, a student at the Russian State University for the Humanities, has visited many places across China. In her view, China has achieved outstanding accomplishments in medicine, robotics, rocket manufacturing and other fields. "While preserving its traditions and history, China has also made tremendous strides in high and new technologies," said Zvereva. ■

item.title: English version of think tank report on China's ecological and environmental code released in Armenia
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
YEREVAN, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- The English version of a think tank report on China's Ecological and Environmental Code was released Wednesday in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. The report, titled "China's Innovations and Global Contributions Through the Ecological and Environmental Code," was released at the China Pavilion during the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17). On the same day, the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization held a side event at the China Pavilion themed "Conserving Biodiversity, Respecting Cultural Diversity and Practicing Multilateralism." The report was among the outcomes highlighting achievements in building a beautiful China that were released at the event. Hu Jun, director of the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, said at the event that China attaches great importance to biodiversity conservation. Guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, China has enacted and implemented the Ecological and Environmental Code, put in place an ecological conservation redline system, established a protected areas system with national parks as the mainstay and carried out major biodiversity conservation projects, continuously improving the diversity, stability and sustainability of ecosystems, he said. The report was jointly compiled by a research team from the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, Xinhua Institute and the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law. The Ecological and Environmental Code of the People's Republic of China took effect on Aug. 15, 2026, when the Chinese version of the report was released by the National High-Level Think Tank of Xinhua News Agency. Also on Wednesday, the English version of another think tank report, "Progress and Achievements in Building a Beautiful Countryside in China," was released at the China Pavilion. It was jointly compiled by researchers from the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, China Daily and China Environment News. ■

item.title: China issues revised administrative measures for outbound investment
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China on Thursday unveiled revised administrative measures for outbound investment, aiming to provide stronger institutional safeguards for its development and security. The measures, released by the National Development and Reform Commission, China's top economic planner, will take effect on Dec. 1, 2026, replacing the existing rules enacted in 2017. China's outbound investment has maintained steady growth in recent years. By the end of 2025, the country's outbound investment stock had reached nearly 3.4 trillion U.S. dollars, keeping China among the world's top three investors for nine consecutive years, data from the Ministry of Commerce showed. ■

item.title: Xi calls for new achievements on new Long March
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a gathering commemorating the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 22, 2026. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei) BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for new achievements on the new Long March as China commemorates the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March. "Only by remembering history can we create a brighter future," said Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, when addressing a gathering held in Beijing to mark the anniversary. Under Xi's proposal, all participants stood up and observed a moment of silence for the revolutionary heroes who gave their lives during the Long March and in revolutionary struggles across China. From October 1934 to October 1936, the Red Army marched through more than 10 provinces during the Long March, opening up a new chapter in the Chinese revolution, Xi said. "This earth-shattering revolutionary feat holds great significance in the history of our Party, country and military, and has a profound impact on our path toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," he noted. Xi stressed that the Party's right leadership and the establishment of Mao Zedong's core position were decisive for the victory of the Red Army's Long March. The Party and the Red Army relied on firm conviction, Xi said, adding that troops with noble ideals and firm beliefs are invincible. Xi emphasized the importance of integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities in addressing the country's issues and problems. He further underscored that the people will always be the source of strength and a strong support for the Party and the people's armed forces. Xi said the great spirit of the Long March demonstrates the power of loyalty, truth, justice and unity. "It will always be a precious treasure and a powerful driving force inspiring us to overcome difficulties and forge ahead courageously." He said the road of the Long March continues to extend. "On our new journey, we are now committed to realizing the Second Centenary Goal of building China into a great modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through a Chinese path to modernization," he said. To forge ahead on the new Long March, Xi said, it is imperative to stay committed to the Party's ideals, convictions and purpose and rely closely on the people to create new achievements. He underscored the need to unswervingly advance high-quality development and promote common prosperity for all. Efforts must be made to better ensure both development and security and seize the historical initiative to overcome difficulties, combat risks and meet challenges, he stressed. Xi also emphasized the importance of moving more quickly to reinforce the people's armed forces to world-class standards and adhering to the Party's absolute leadership over the military. It is also vital to uphold the leadership of the Party, strengthen Party building and persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance, he added. Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, as well as Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, attended the gathering. Zhao, who presided over the event, said Xi's speech was of immense political, ideological and guiding significance, urging earnest efforts to study and grasp its essence and ensure its effective implementation. He called on the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups to rally more closely around the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization. Around 3,000 people participated in the gathering at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. ■ A gathering commemorating the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March is held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 22, 2026.
